_meta.note: Indices mirror the FR file exactly: 0=Sunday, 1=Monday, ..., 6=Saturday.

monday: The week begins. Today's choices write Friday's.
A new page. No one will write it for you, {firstName}.
Monday is not a constraint. It is an appointment with your best self.
Seven days lie ahead. Only one truly counts: this one.
To start tomorrow is the art of never starting at all.
The week ahead is a promise. Keep it.
Your body cannot tell Monday from Saturday. You can. Decide.
The true luxury is consistency. Grant yourself that luxury, {firstName}.
What you rehearse on Monday, you master by Sunday.
Nothing happens by halves. Not the week that begins.
A successful Monday is not intense. It is precise.
Intention, not perfection. Set yours now.
Every Monday is a chance to refuse the almost-good-enough.
Discipline does not wait for the mood. It precedes it.
You know the road. You need only take the first step.
tuesday: Tuesday rewards those who held the line on Monday. That is you.
You recognise an athlete by their Tuesdays, never by their Mondays.
Consistency is a form of elegance. It is not seen, it is felt.
It is not the perfect session that counts. It is the session done.
Your body is keeping record. Even without the spectacular. Above all without the spectacular.
On Tuesday, Monday's promises turn into habits.
Two consecutive days. That is already a trajectory.
True work is quiet. Yours is, {firstName}.
Progress loves repetition. It dislikes improvisation.
Today, be precise. Not severe. Precise.
One right effort is worth ten approximate ones.
Fatigue is not an obstacle. It is a signal.
What seems ordinary today will look remarkable in three months.
Tuesday is the real test of commitment. You are passing it.
Do not count your sessions. Make each session count.
wednesday: In the middle of the week, you see who is truly committed.
Wednesday is a border. Those who cross it go far.
No slackening. No surging. Only continuity.
Three days of effort is already a signature.
It is not the summit that is hard. It is the middle slope.
Your week will resemble the decisions you make today.
On Wednesday, you stop thinking "begin" and start thinking "continue".
Consistency is built precisely here, in the middle.
You are at the halfway point. Too late to doubt, not too late to adjust.
Honour the plan. It was built for this week, not for your mood.
Real strength is doing what was planned when nothing forces you to.
One more day. Then another. That is how a life is changed.
Today is not an average day. It is a decisive one.
The middle of the week is not negotiated. It is crossed.
You are already ahead of the person you were on Monday.
thursday: Thursday is the day sessions count twice: in fatigue, and in meaning.
You are closing in. Do not slow down. Tighten up.
Today's effort weighs more than yesterday's. That is normal. That is good.
Four days held. You are the reference now, {firstName}.
A tired body progresses better than a fresh one, provided it is respected.
Great weeks are won on Thursdays.
Today, ask yourself: am I executing, or am I performing?
The effort that costs you nothing has not yet begun.
Today's quality will be read in your results six weeks from now.
On Thursday, we stop talking. We do.
Your consistency since Monday is a rare act. Honour it.
Seven days make a week. Four days already make a commitment.
People do not quit at the start or the end. They quit on Thursday. Not you.
What you do today, your body will remember six months from now.
The threshold is not physical. It is mental. You are on the right side of it.
friday: You are reaching the end. Neither first day nor last. Decisive.
Friday is the day of the final ten percent. The part that makes the difference.
Finishing a week like this one is already an achievement.
No pre-weekend letting go. The week is not yet done.
On Friday evening, you will want to remember this Friday morning.
Five days. You are an example to the person you were on Monday.
Accumulated fatigue is the finest fuel for a clean effort.
You did not come this far for nothing. Close the week as you opened it.
Today, close your week the way one closes a contract: with care.
Friday is a ritual. Respect it, {firstName}.
What you finish today will carry you through the weekend.
The best weeks are the ones whose Friday resembles their Monday.
The last effort of the week is also the most meaningful.
Finish strong. Rest will only feel more earned.
You are sturdier than on day one. That, precisely, is progress.
saturday: Saturday is an art: the art of resting without losing oneself.
True relaxation is not excess. It is the chosen moment.
What you do on Saturday counts as much as what you do on Tuesday.
A chosen indulgence is worth more than ten you did not choose.
The weekend is not a parenthesis. It is a continuation.
Thoughtful pleasure ruins nothing. It enriches everything.
A recovery day is never a lost day.
Saturday morning says much about the week just past. And about the one to come.
To recover is not to stop. It is to choose another kind of effort.
The body calls for rest as the mind calls for reading. Respect that.
Today, eat well. Move gently. Breathe fully.
A clear-headed Saturday prepares a serene Sunday.
Pleasure, yes. Drift, no. You know the difference.
Rest is an ingredient. Not an exception.
sunday: On Sunday, we look back without nostalgia. And ahead without haste.
One week ends. Another takes shape. Everything lives in the interval.
Sunday is a day of tidying, mental as much as physical.
What you prepare today spares you from improvising on Monday.
Take some time for yourself, {firstName}. You have earned it.
One quiet Sunday is worth a thousand chaotic weeks.
Breathe. The week past is engraved. The one to come is still to be written.
Anticipate without rushing. That is the finest form of mastery.
Sunday is the day of calm decisions.
Look over your plan for the week. Be proud to have held it.
Before you project, savour. The present counts too.
True performance is also nourished by these days without performance.
A Sunday well lived is already a Monday well begun.
Slow down. It is, at times, the highest form of discipline.
Review, accept, begin again. The Sunday triptych.
training_day: A session awaits today. Approach it as you would a serious appointment.
The body is ready. So is the mind, if you decide it is.
No perfect sessions. Only sessions done. Do this one, {firstName}.
Prepare yourself physically. Prepare yourself mentally. Both matter.
Today's programme is not an obligation. It is a tool.
Ten minutes of warm-up spare you six months of injury.
Every working set performed cleanly is a set won.
Breathe, ground yourself, begin. The rest will follow.
You are not chasing performance. You are chasing precision.
Today, be the athlete you quietly admire.
rest_day: Rest day. It is part of the plan. Honour it as you would a session.
Muscle does not grow during the effort. It grows now.
Sleeping well is an invisible session. Sleep well tonight.
Eat cleanly. Hydrate. Walk a little. That is your real training today.
Rest is never a luxury. It is a requirement.
Today your body thanks you for yesterday and prepares for tomorrow.
Nothing to force. Nothing to prove. Only to recover, {firstName}.
One day of intelligent recovery is worth three sloppy sessions.

3: Three days in a row. A habit is beginning to take root, {firstName}.
7: Seven days. A full week without breaking the line. That is rare.
Seven consecutive days. You have just crossed the border.
14: Two weeks. This is no longer an attempt. It is a way of life.
Fourteen days. You are officially consistent.
21: Twenty-one days. The number said to belong to habit. You are there, {firstName}.
30: Thirty days. This is no longer motivation. It is discipline.
A full month. You are not the same person you were thirty days ago.
50: Fifty days. This is what separates those who try from those who do.
60: Two months. Your body and your choices are no longer strangers, {firstName}.
100: One hundred days. Few ever reach this number. You have.
One hundred days. You have crossed into the territory of the serious.
200: Two hundred days. At this stage, we no longer speak of effort. We speak of identity.
365: One year. A full year without letting go. You have become the reference, {firstName}.
